notes.author: user
notes.text: Make authentication independently switchable from the GUI for the Web dashboard and MCP.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Reprioritized under the 2026-09-05 owner-first, reusable-experiment direction. Revisit for a concrete workflow that needs independent modes. Avoid adding an authentication state machine solely to support hypothetical deployment variants.

problem: Web pairing-token authentication and MCP bearer authentication are always enabled and configured outside the dashboard. Operators cannot independently choose the appropriate authentication mode, see its effective exposure, or safely enable and disable each boundary from one control surface.

risk.rollback: Restore Web pairing-token mode and MCP scoped-token mode, close anonymous sessions, and rotate credentials. A rollback must fail closed rather than leave either listener anonymous.

scope: Add separate Web and MCP authentication controls to a security settings screen. Show the effective bind address, transport security, authentication mode, active sessions, and a persistent warning whenever either boundary is unauthenticated.
Support Web modes pairing-token, local-accounts, and disabled. Support MCP modes scoped-tokens and disabled-authentication while retaining a separate switch for disabling the MCP listener entirely.

Treat authentication-mode changes as high-risk mutations: require an admin re-authentication or current pairing credential, an explicit confirmation describing affected clients, and an audit event. Do not let an ordinary user or MCP client change these modes.

Keep MCP bound to loopback even when MCP authentication is disabled. Disabling MCP authentication must close existing sessions, clear their transport authorization state, and leave reservations to their documented expiry/release behavior rather than silently transferring ownership.

Permit disabled Web authentication on loopback with a prominent banner. On a non-loopback listener, require controller HTTPS plus an explicit insecure-mode confirmation; otherwise refuse the change instead of exposing process control anonymously over plaintext LAN HTTP.

Protect the security-settings mutation itself even while ordinary Web authentication is disabled: require an existing admin password or a short-lived recovery code generated by the local CLI, so an anonymous visitor cannot enable a new mode, create the first admin, or lock out the operator.

Validate transitions before committing them: account mode requires an enabled admin, scoped MCP mode requires at least one usable admin-created token or an atomic token-creation flow, and disabling the last recovery path is rejected.

Apply changes atomically and report whether browser sessions, MCP sessions, pairing links, and tokens were invalidated. Provide CLI recovery and status commands, but keep ordinary enable/disable controls available in the GUI as requested.
title: Control Web and MCP authentication independently
trigger: Revisit for a concrete workflow that needs independent modes. Avoid adding an authentication state machine solely to support hypothetical deployment variants.
validation: Switch Web independently among pairing-token, local-accounts, and disabled while MCP remains unchanged, then switch MCP authentication without changing Web mode.
Verify every transition requires the appropriate current administrator/recovery credential, is audited, and cannot be performed by a normal user, anonymous caller, or MCP token.
Verify MCP remains loopback-only without authentication and existing sessions cannot retain stale capabilities after an authentication-mode transition.
Verify plaintext non-loopback Web cannot enter disabled or password-account mode without the documented secure transport and explicit override controls.
Verify the GUI cannot activate account mode without an admin, activate scoped MCP mode without a recovery credential, or remove the last working recovery path.
Verify the status screen and MCP status expose effective modes and warnings without revealing password hashes, bearer tokens, cookies, reset values, or private configuration.
value: Operators can choose different security postures for human and agent access without conflating Web sessions, MCP credentials, or listener availability.
